method.closeMethod: On the same thread, immediately after the selected fully decoded event yields, call response[EventStream].close(), then close that dedicated boto3 client with client.close(). No socket shutdown monkeypatch, iterator continuation, reconnect, admission retry, or additional SubscribeToShard call for that consumer. Record raw HTTP response, connection and captured socket states on either side.
method.frameTimeMeaning: Client UTC and monotonic time immediately after SDK yields decoded frame, not service publication timestamp.
method.postCloseVisibility: Cannot directly observe service frames after client socket closure. Native per-minute metrics can establish continued service-side samples, not packets received by a closed client or exact internal disconnect-detection timing.

queryWindow.note: Fixed whole-minute window spans before both subscriptions through at least three minutes after latest ordinary 300s subscription horizon. No records are written.

extendedQueryWindow.purpose: Supplement fixed long-lag rechecks with all elapsed minutes while resources were kept alive, including cleanup minute. Missing datapoints remain bounded to this query/retrieval time; late arrivals beyond final observation are not excluded.

evidencedSemantics: For these two isolated empty-shard early-disconnect runs, no SubscribeToShardEvent.Success zero sample was returned in any recheck; all Success samples had value 1.

Native Success and companion frame metric sample counts exceeded decoded client frames by one in each run (2 vs 1 and 8 vs 7). Therefore client-decoded frame count is not guaranteed to equal service metric sample count.

No metric buckets after each close minute were returned, despite keeping the stream and both consumers ACTIVE through the ordinary five-minute horizon plus 900 seconds. Early-close observations do not support sustained heartbeat metric publication until the natural horizon.

An SDK close returned after closing the captured real SSL socket in both runs; neither run observed natural EOF, a service error frame, or a client exception. These results must not be modeled as natural EOF evidence.
uncertainty: One run per early-close point; no claim that every disconnection behaves identically.

One-minute CloudWatch aggregates cannot place the extra service sample precisely before/after socket closure, distinguish buffered/in-flight events from a post-close publication attempt, or measure exact server disconnect-detection time.

After closing the socket, client receipt of further frames is unavailable by construction. Continued service frame transmission itself is not directly observed; metric observations only establish service sample counts and minute buckets.
No zero Success samples were observed here through final long-lag recheck; this does not rule out zeros for other disconnect circumstances, error paths, or publication after the final retrieval.
No semantics of natural five-minute EOF are inferred from these explicit early client closes.
